clue.text: One very loudly breaking singer's jaw

indicators.note: breaking into the singer's name, so the other pieces sit inside it

parts.note: Cher is the famous one-named pop singer
one gives A, the indefinite article
FF is fortissimo, the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone sings so loudly it puts a singer's jaw out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jaw' looks like the body part; here it is a verb, to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaffer is to chatter or haggle, and jaw is slang for idle talk, so both mean to natter.

clue.text: Successful striker won't start — it makes Jonathan lose heart

indicators.note: won't start means the striker loses its first letter

parts.note: a scorer is a striker who puts the ball in the net

explanation.surface: A goalscorer, off the team sheet, leaves Jonathan heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan is a variety of apple, not a man: a corer takes out its core, its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A corer is a kitchen tool that removes the core of an apple such as the Jonathan variety.

clue.text: What may be employed by summer time — underwear to keep cool, at last

definitions.text: What may be employed by summer

indicators.note: to keep means the time piece holds another letter inside

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of cool

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: In summer time, underwear that keeps you cool at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts L inside AGE. 'summer' is one who sums, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is a branch of mathematics, so someone doing sums might use it.

clue.text: Iron-clad soldiers look out

indicators.note: clad means the iron piece wraps around the soldiers

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers in armour plating keep watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron-clad' reads as one adjective but splits into the iron piece and its container indicator. Fore is the golfer's warning shout.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer shouts fore to warn people to look out for the ball.

clue.text: Pour artist small drinks included at beach party by the gallon

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the artist and small swallow the rest

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
S is short for small, as on clothing labels
inc. is an abbreviation for included
sand covers a beach
a do is a party

explanation.surface: An artist pours small drinks at a beach party, by the gallon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks' wraps the artist and small around everything from 'included' to 'gallon'; 'by the' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rain cats and dogs is an idiom for raining very hard, i.e. to pour down.

clue.text: Leonard and Alfred briefly returned the sweet talk

indicators.note: returned says the whole string of names is read back to front

parts.note: Len is a short form of Leonard
'n' is the clipped form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
Alf is the short form of Alfred

explanation.surface: Two men, Len and Alf, come back with smooth flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LEN + N + ALF into FLANNEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel is British slang for smooth, flattering or evasive talk, the same as sweet talk.

clue.text: Images in which 3 ate and 14, too?

definitions.meaning: images are figurative expressions like metaphors
the answers to 3 and 14 and the word ate all sound like numbers, so they are figures spoken

explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is FORE (four), ate sounds like eight, and 14 across is NAUGHT (nought): all spoken numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures of speech are metaphors and similes, i.e. verbal images; read literally they are numbers that are spoken.

clue.text: Erotic experience is a drag, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that we hear the words said, not read them

parts.note: traction is a pulling or dragging, so a drag is a traction

explanation.surface: Sexual experience is boring, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' looks like slang for something tedious; it is pulling, i.e. traction.
explanation.definitionFit: Attraction is the feeling of being drawn to someone, here a sexual experience.

clue.text: Cynical racist stance?

definitions.meaning: cynical, dark and disillusioned, as in film noir
the old landlord's sign '...' was a racist stance

explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO IRISH, the slogan on prejudiced British boarding-house signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Noirish describes the dark, world-weary tone of film noir, which is cynical.

clue.text: Canvas used by sailor having earache?

definitions.meaning: a sail is canvas used by a sailor

explanation.definitionFit: A lugsail is a four-sided sail hung from a yard, canvas used on boats.

clue.text: Having a look about

definitions.meaning: to regard is to look at, so this is looking
about as a preposition means concerning or with respect to

explanation.definitionFit: Regard is to look at something, and as a preposition the word means concerning, a sense of about.

clue.text: Article obtained with spare thousand dollars

parts.note: spare as an adjective means lean or thin
G is a grand, slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: Something got hold of with a lean grand in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is any object or item, which is what a thing is.

clue.text: What frotteur does with unknown girl

parts.note: a frotteur gets pleasure from rubbing against people
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A creepy rubber and a girl he doesn't know.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a girl's first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Italian composer wasted time once rejecting an infantile complaint

indicators.note: wasted means one piece of the composer's name is lost

parts.note: Domenico (or Alessandro) Scarlatti were Italian composers
T is the abbreviation for time, removed only once of the two

indicators.note: rejecting turns the word an back to front

explanation.surface: An Italian composer, once wasting time, turns down an illness of childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' removes one T from SCARLATTI, giving SCARLATI; 'rejecting' turns AN into NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlatina, a mild scarlet fever, is an illness mostly caught by young children.

clue.text: Vain like Gregory?

definitions.meaning: the name Gregory has the word ego in its centre

explanation.definitionFit: An egocentric person thinks only of themselves, which is what vain describes.

clue.text: Barton ultimately a thug, irritating FA

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the name Barton
irritating suggests the words a thug are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Footballer Joey Barton, in the end a thug, annoying the Football Association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritating' rearranges A THUG into AUGHT. FA here is 'sweet FA', British slang for nothing at all; Joey Barton is a footballer known for violent conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet FA is a British euphemism meaning nothing whatsoever, i.e. zero.

clue.text: Argentinian poster boy posed at first with hand bag

indicators.note: at first puts the posing piece before the Argentinian

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so posed gives sat
Che Guevara, born in Argentina, is the face on countless posters
L stands for left, as in the left hand

explanation.surface: Che Guevara first sat for a picture holding a handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: Che Guevara was born in Argentina; his face is the classic student-bedroom poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a bag with a shoulder strap, typically carried by schoolchildren.

clue.text: Travelling west, Slav spies Italian city

indicators.note: in an across clue, travelling west means reading the Slav right to left

parts.note: a Serb is one of the Slavic peoples
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A Slavic spy heading west to an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling west' turns SERB into BRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a city in Lombardy in northern Italy.

clue.text: Pick-up location where you get kiss — great!

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
top means excellent, great

explanation.surface: Where you get a kiss: great for a pick-up spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus stop is where passengers are picked up by a bus.

clue.text: Letter supporting English boy, who gets expelled

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below the other pieces

parts.note: Vic is a boy's name
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T

explanation.surface: A letter backing an English lad who is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts TEE beneath E + VIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictee is someone evicted, forced out of a home.

clue.text: Slack dandy stealing Helen's heart with heartless ploy

indicators.note: the dandy steals, taking the letter inside himself

parts.note: a fop is a dandy, a man vain about clothes

indicators.note: heart picks the central letter of the name Helen
heartless strips away the middle letters of ploy, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A slick dandy stealing Helen's heart with an unfeeling trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stealing' puts Helen's central letter into the dandy; 'heartless' keeps only the outer letters of ploy.
explanation.definitionFit: Floppy means hanging loose and limp, which is what slack describes.

clue.text: Sort of wine salesman raised alarm

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the pieces are written upwards

parts.note: brut is a dry kind of sparkling wine
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A wine salesman raises the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns BRUT + REP into PERTURB. 'alarm' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb is to disturb or worry, which is what to alarm means.

clue.text: In the main, reveals all the low-fat party food?

definitions.meaning: swims in the sea (the main) naked, showing everything
skinny as slimmed-down food, and dips as party nibbles

explanation.definitionFit: Skinny-dipping is bathing naked, and dips with skinny read as low-fat would be slimmers' party food.

clue.text: One's inclined to the left — or to right? To the left

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading to the left means writing the pieces backwards

parts.note: to is taken as written

explanation.surface: Is someone leaning left or right? Left, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the left' turns TO + RT into TROT. Trot is short for Trotskyist, a hard-left socialist; 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trot is a Trotskyist, a follower of Trotsky, so one politically inclined to the left.

clue.text: Fill pot

parts.note: the word top written upwards, as in a down entry, reads pot

explanation.surface: Fill the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the wordplay is in the answer, telling you to put TOP upwards, which gives the clue word pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up is to refill a glass or tank, so to fill.

clue.text: Excitement makes you cooler

definitions.meaning: cooler and ... are both slang for prison

explanation.definitionFit: Stir means commotion, and also prison, as does cooler.

clue.text: School of trout swimming

indicators.note: swimming suggests the fish's letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A school of trout swimming along.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach them, which is to tutor them.

clue.text: Public gets behind what a card player may do

definitions.text: what a card player may do

parts.note: overt means open and public
the rump is the behind, the backside

explanation.surface: The public gets behind the moves of a card player.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrump is to play a higher trump than one already played, a move in whist or bridge.

clue.text: Bores perhaps writing cutting articles

indicators.note: cutting means one piece slices into the other

parts.note: pieces are articles, as in newspaper pieces
writing is one of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic), so R; perhaps flags it as an example

explanation.surface: Dull people, perhaps, writing scathing newspaper articles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts R inside PIECES. 'Bores' is a verb here, not dull people.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore through something is to drill a hole in it, which is what piercing does.

clue.text: Sort of jazz instrument holds back from loud hum

indicators.note: holds says the instrument contains the other pieces

parts.note: the harp is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: back from points to the final letter of loud

parts.note: hum is slang for a bad smell, as is BO, body odour

explanation.surface: An instrument holds back from making a loud humming noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hum' is British slang for a bad smell, not a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard bop is a style of 1950s jazz developed from bebop.
